newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE, S.AFRICA EXTRADITION TALKS STALLED.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE, S.AFRICA EXTRADITION TALKS STALLED.

text.p: Long-running extradition talks between Zimbabwe and South Africa have hit a snag over demands by Pretoria that Harare should not administer the death penalty on extradited prisoners, the Financial Gazette reported on Thursday.

It quoted Home Affairs Minister Dumiso Dabengwa as saying South Africa was concerned that it might violate its own laws against the death penalty if it released murder convicts to Zimbabwe where they might be executed.
Dabengwa was unavailable for further comment on Thursday.
The two southern African countries were initially scheduled to conclude negotiations on an extradition treaty in 1995.
"The death penalty in Zimbabwe's statute books is the only obstacle to the treaty," Dabengwa said.
"Pretoria has said it will not be party to a treaty that could result in prisoners extradited from South Africa being sentenced to death in Zimbabwe's courts," he said.
He however said Zimbabwe had prepared a compromise to accommodate Pretoria's demands and the two countries planned to meet soon to discuss it.

South Africa scrapped the death penalty soon after its historic all-race elections in 1994 but the Zimbabwean government is resisting calls from human rights organisations to abolish capital punishment.
